headsInThisRound.why: This round's code was written at 39175757c326, which carried the review App as its author. I found that while checking the delta, the architect ruled it a record defect worth a round, and the implementer rewrote the commit as d4de531733a9 with its own identity. Every measurement below says which head it was taken at; the two heads are the same content, proved under identityCheck.

implementerProof.how: Every claim of the two handoffs this round covers was re-run here. The role work at 39175757c326 and again, unchanged, at the rewritten d4de531733a9: the refused startup claim and its retry, both sweep rules kept apart with their controls, the unparseable record, and the touch. The media-query claim I drove myself with a Chromium launch flag rather than reading its number. The page claim I checked by its delta first, as the architect asked: this round's own commit touches nothing under packages/dispatch, so the Agents spec in both profiles is the scope and round three's whole-project evidence stands for the markup. The rewrite round's own proof — that it changed identity and nothing else — I did not take from its handoff: I read it from the repository myself, under identityCheck.

proof.criterion: Finding 1: a soft role claim refused at startup is retried on the heartbeat, and a refusal that repeats is retried again.
proof.surface: The committed dist/envoy-channel.js run as Claude Code runs it, against a real nats-server with JetStream and an Envoy listener built from this tree, behind a proxy of my own that answers 503 to the first two POSTs of /v1/roles/set and forwards everything else.
proof.command: a tester probe (/tmp/r4-role.sh with /tmp/r4-proxy.ts, deleted after the round), case A; the holder read from the listener's own GET /v1/roles/planner
proof.observed: The session alive, the proxy recording refusals=2, one stderr line — 'envoy-channel: could not restore the role from <…>/roles/a-0001.json (POST …/v1/roles/set failed with 503: injected listener outage); the next heartbeat retries' — and the listener answering holder=a-0001 after the retries. Two refusals, so a one-shot retry would not have reached the holder.
proof.negativeControl: The same probe's later cases run the same path with the proxy refusing nothing: the claim lands at startup, no retry line is written, and the holder is named without any heartbeat.

proof.criterion: The architect's rule — the sweep must never delete the record of the session running it — holds, and the sweep still deletes an abandoned record in the same run.
proof.surface: The same live rig, one roles directory holding two records of identical age, swept by the session that owns one of them.
proof.command: the same probe, case B1: a 31-day-old record of the starting session whose claim the proxy refuses once, an identically aged abandoned record beside it, then the startup sweep and the heartbeats
proof.observed: Before: own=31.0 days, abandoned=31.0 days. After the refused claim, the startup sweep that follows it and the heartbeats: the own record kept and refreshed to 0.0, the abandoned record gone, holder=b1-0001 — so the role was recovered from the record the sweep would have deleted.
proof.negativeControl: The abandoned record itself: identical age, identical shape, same directory, same sweep, deleted. What kept the other one is the condition on the session id and not a sweep that stopped deleting.

proof.criterion: Finding 2, kept apart from the rule above: a long-held record survives a sweep run by a different session only because the heartbeat refreshes it.
proof.surface: The same rig: a session holding its role against the real listener, its record and an abandoned one both aged to 31 days while it runs, then a second session whose startup sweep runs as someone else.
proof.observed: Aged under the live holder: live=31.0, abandoned=31.0, holder=b2-0001. After two heartbeats: live=0.0, abandoned=31.0 — only the live holder's record was touched. After the second session's startup sweep: live kept, abandoned gone.
proof.negativeControl: The abandoned record, identically aged at the start and swept by that same foreign sweep, deleted. The two rules therefore pass for their own reasons: B1's record is saved by the session-id condition with no heartbeat in it, B2's by the refresh with no condition in it, and neither case could have passed on the other's mechanism.

proof.criterion: The kept record is a record a live session keeps, not a record nothing can ever remove (the architect's resume case).
proof.surface: The same rig, with a record carrying the running session's id but written by an earlier process and never touched by this one.
proof.command: the same probe, case B3: the record aged to 31 days before the session starts, then the session stopped, the record aged again, and another session's startup sweep run over it
proof.observed: While that session ran: resume=0.0 (kept, then refreshed), the abandoned control gone, holder=b3-0001. With that session gone and the record aged again to 31.0: a sweep by another session deleted it. So the record is unsweepable only while its own session runs, which is the whole of the rule and none of a leak.
proof.negativeControl: The same record before that second sweep, at 31.0 days and present: the deletion is the sweep's doing and not the session's exit.

proof.criterion: The failure shapes around the role record cost the session its role and nothing else, and the heartbeat's touch leaves nothing beside the record.
proof.surface: The same rig: an unparseable record, a record at mode 000, the roles directory at mode 000, a directory standing where the record should be, and fifteen seconds of listings of roles/ during heartbeats.
proof.command: the same probe, cases C and D, and a second tester probe (/tmp/r4-guard.sh, deleted after the round) for the three permission shapes
proof.observed: The unparseable record: alive, exactly one stderr line over twelve seconds — so it is not queued and does not spin — and the record untouched. Mode 000 on the record, mode 000 on the directory, and a directory in its place: each alive, registered under its chosen name, and taking a later rename within the heartbeat, with one stderr line naming the file and the reason (EACCES, EACCES, EISDIR). Sixty listings of roles/ over fifteen seconds of one-second heartbeats showed one name and only one, the record itself: the touch drops no temporary file for a directory listing to catch.
proof.negativeControl: The same bundle with a well-formed readable record in the same probe: no stderr line at all and the role claimed at startup, so the single line is the failure being reported once and not noise the server always writes.

proof.criterion: Finding 3: the row's media query and its md: classes answer alike at a root font size other than 16 px.
proof.surface: Dispatch's own browser suite in a real Chromium launched twice with --blink-settings=defaultFontSize=16 and =20, at an 800 px viewport — between 768 px as an absolute number and 48rem, which is 960 px at the larger root.
proof.command: a throwaway spec of mine (packages/dispatch/e2e/zz-rem-probe.e2e.ts, run in the chromium project and deleted) that reads both media queries, the computed root font size, and the row's rendered directory
proof.observed: root 16px: computed root=16px, (min-width:768px)=true, (min-width:48rem)=true, directory 192x16 reading 'build-host · features' — the laptop layout, agreed by both. root 20px: computed root=20px, (min-width:768px)=true, (min-width:48rem)=false, directory 708x20 reading the whole path — the below-md layout, which is where the md: classes are at that width too. The predicate and the classes now answer alike where they used to disagree.
proof.negativeControl: The old constant measured in the same run: (min-width: 768px) answers true at root 20px, which is the divergence — the shortened directory inside the layout meant to keep the whole path — that the rem value removes.

proof.criterion: Nothing on the Agents page moved, and the plugin still registers the name a person gave the session.
proof.surface: Dispatch's browser suite in a real Chromium, the Agents spec in the chromium and iphone projects; and the committed bundles against a real nats-server and Envoy listener.
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/dispatch_e2e_c ./node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts e2e/agents.e2e.ts --project chromium --project iphone; then bash packages/claude-envoy/scripts/smoke-session-title.sh
proof.observed: 34 passed, 0 failed (3.4 minutes), the row at :1717 and my round-two red row at :1807 green in both profiles. The smoke PASS, all four cases: 'eeny meeny', then 'miny moe', then 'probe-project smoke-ti', with the dispatch stamp holding 'miny moe'.
proof.negativeControl: The smoke's own last case: main@origin's dist/envoy-channel.js registered the folder-and-short-id fallback and not the chosen name.
proof.scopeNote: The Agents spec rather than the whole chromium and iphone projects, on the architect's instruction and my own check of the delta: this round's commit touches nothing under packages/dispatch, and the only page change since round three's whole-project runs is the one media-query constant over markup those runs proved. Round three's 720/617/4 project runs are the evidence for the markup; they are not re-run here.

identityCheck.why: I raised the record defect, so the architect asked that I verify its fix myself rather than cite the implementer's: a record defect verified only by the role that made it is the same shape of mistake as a guard that covers one of two commits.
identityCheck.rewriteChangedIdentityAlone: git rev-parse 39175757c326^{tree} and d4de531733a9^{tree} both read ba5069e1951b10ae229b293162c0b8e79fb85ab1; both have parent 898037479328; their messages are byte-identical including the Omp-Session trailer; and git diff 39175757c326 d4de531733a9 is empty. So the plugin numbers measured at the old commit are numbers at the new one.
identityCheck.branchAudit: git log --format='%h A=%ae C=%ce' main..0a853016 over every commit of the branch: each code commit and each implement handoff is legion-implementer[bot] in both columns; each plan, test and review handoff is legion-reviewer[bot] in both columns, which is right, since the planner, tester and reviewer all carry the review App. No commit mixes the two, and the one that did (39175757c326, author legion-reviewer[bot], committer legion-implementer[bot]) is gone from the branch.
identityCheck.cause: My own round-three push left an empty working-copy commit authored by the review App; the implementer split that commit rather than starting a new one, which keeps the author and takes the splitter as committer. skill://legion-worker warns against exactly that, and handoff_complete refuses a handoff carried by another App's commit — but nothing checks a code commit, which is why the defect showed on one of the two. That asymmetry belongs in the retro learning.

notProven: That Claude Code itself sends session_title, and that the daemon's seeded '/rename Legion <role> · <KEY>' (packages/daemon/internal/claudebridge/bridge.go:196-198) makes a pane read as its role and issue. Claude Code cannot run in a Legion issue pod, so every hook payload in every run here is JSON the harness writes in the documented shape.

The webkit, webkit-iphone, firefox and firefox-download-navigation projects: Playwright's host validation refuses to start those engines in this pod for want of system libraries no agent can install without root. CI carries them.
A session whose Envoy or inbound messages are off stamps its title once at startup, so a later rename does not reach its Dispatch attribution. Unchanged behaviour for every title, not this change's.
knownNotThisChange: packages/dispatch/e2e/phone.e2e.ts:393, dispatch://INFRA-95's row, which was red three times of three in round three. Its fix, sjawhar/legion#2156, merged to main at 09:26Z after this branch's base; I re-ran that row six times on a throwaway clone of main at 14571f6f4aea and it passed six times of six, so the fix holds in a pod and this branch's red will go when the base comes in at the merge. Nothing of it is this change's.
packages/claude-envoy's 'queryTmux is bounded even by a tmux that ignores SIGTERM': the gVisor spawn-timeout host behaviour the stream lead settled as a retro learning.
